topics.title: The hook: this has never happened before
topics.why_now: Bitcoin touched its 200-week SMA on Nov 13 for the second time this year, with a bull market in between, and Sunday's weekly close decides whether it is back in a bear market.
topics.angle: Your face, your title, what is at stake on Sunday. Say the sequence in one breath: bear market, 200-week, bull market, bear market, 200-week. All in 2026.

prompts: This has never happened before. Not this fast. Bitcoin hit the 200-week in June, went into a bull market in September, and this week it's right back on the 200-week.
And Sunday's close decides if we're officially back in a bear market. Let me show you why that matters.

topics.title: Sunday decides: the 50-week
topics.why_now: BTC is around 9% under its 50-week SMA after 7 weekly closes above it, and last Sunday closed right on the line.
topics.angle: Your own definition, from your Nov 2 stream: two weekly closes below the 50-week is a bear market. Show the line, say the number Sunday has to beat, and say what happens if it doesn't.

tabs.label: BTC weekly: Sunday's line (50-week SMA)
tabs.show: Add the 50-week SMA. Hover this week's candle and read the line's value, then point at the Sep 20 to Nov 1 closes above it.
prompts: This is the line. The 50-week. Bitcoin closed above it seven weeks in a row, from September 20 to November 1. That's the bull market everybody got excited about.
Last Sunday closed right on it. Now we're around 9% under it. To stay above it, Sunday has to close above around 75,200.
My definition of a bear market is two weekly closes below the 50-week. If Sunday closes under it, that's it. And when that happens, it can go a lot further down.

facts.text: Sunday's line: a weekly close above around 75,180 keeps BTC over its 50-week SMA (CoinDesk had the SMA at $75,153 on Nov 12). BTC was 68,371 on Nov 13, 9.1% under it
facts.source: computed from BTC daily closes (Yahoo, scripts/market_data.py), Sunday weekly closes

facts.text: Weekly closes above the 50-week SMA: Sep 20 to Nov 1, 7 in a row. Nov 8 closed at 74,585 against a 75,485 SMA, 1.2% under on Yahoo's closes. blockchain.com's average price has that week just over its line
facts.source: computed from BTC daily closes (Yahoo) and blockchain.com average daily prices

facts.text: 'Bitcoin is on course for its sixth consecutive weekly decline. The record is nine weeks, set in 2022.' Down 21% so far in 2026

careful: The data feeds disagree on whether Nov 8 closed under the line. Read last Sunday's candle off your own chart before you call Sunday 'the second close'. On the Nov 9 stream you said it was still hanging above.
By your definition, one close under the line is a warning and two is the bear market. Keep 'if' in the sentence until Sunday has closed.

topics.title: This has never happened before: back at the 200-week in the same year
topics.why_now: BTC closed under its 200-week SMA for three single weeks between Jun 28 and Aug 16, rallied into a bull market by late September, and touched the 200-week again on Nov 13.
topics.angle: The title moment. Scroll back to June, say 'we are here', then come forward to this week. The sequence happened once before, from December 2018 to March 2020, and it took 15 months. This year it took around four and a half. It is also a problem for the four-year cycle story you reject: one winter every four years does not explain two in one year.

tabs.label: BTC weekly: we are here (the 200-week)
tabs.show: We are here: add the 50-week and 200-week SMA. Pre-scroll this tab to June to August 2026 before you record, circle the three weekly closes under the 200-week, then drag forward through the September reclaim to this week's candle sitting on the 200-week.
prompts: Look at June. Bitcoin went under the 200-week. That's crypto winter. It closed under it three times this summer, and every time it came right back the next week.
Then September, back above the 50-week. A bull market. And now look. We are here. Right back on the 200-week, in the same year.
The only other time Bitcoin did this, 200-week, bull market, bear market, 200-week again, it took 15 months. December 2018 to March 2020. This year it took around four and a half months.

facts.text: 2026: weekly closes under the 200-week SMA on Jun 28 (59,532 against 62,440), Aug 2 and Aug 16, each back above it the next week. The 2026 low close was 58,559 on Jun 30
facts.source: computed from BTC daily closes (Yahoo), Sunday weekly closes

facts.text: Nov 13: 'Bitcoin fell to its 200-week simple moving average at $67,993' (TradingView data), the first time since mid-August

Since 2014, the only other bear market, 200-week, bull market, bear market, 200-week sequence: 200-week in Dec 2018, bull market from May 2019, 200-week again in Mar 2020, 15 months. In 2023 BTC came back to the 200-week while still above its 50-week, so there was no new bear market
facts.source: computed from blockchain.com average daily prices since 2010 (media/bitcoin-update/research/btc-long/)

careful: Say 'never this fast' or 'never in the same year' when you explain the title. The same sequence happened once before over 15 months, so a bare 'never' needs that qualifier.
This week's touch is intraday so far. The weekly close is Sunday, and TradingView, Yahoo and blockchain.com put the 200-week a few hundred dollars apart.

tabs.label: Every bear market since 2014: where it started
prompts: Every bear market since 2014 started way above the 200-week. Bitcoin had to fall another 37 to 61% just to get down there.
Except one. March 2020. That bear market was confirmed right next to the 200-week, and that week was the bottom. This one is starting right on top of it.
inspiring: Last time a bear market started this close to the 200-week, Bitcoin was up 838% a year later. I'm not saying that happens again. I'm saying this isn't the setup everybody thinks it is.

facts.text: Bear markets confirmed since 2014 (the 2nd weekly close under the 50-week), then the lowest weekly close before the next bull market: Aug 2014 -60%, Jun 2018 -58%, Jan 2022 -61%, Nov 2025 -37%. Dec 2019 and Mar 2020: that week was the low
facts.source: computed from blockchain.com average daily prices since 2010 (media/bitcoin-update/research/btc-long/)

facts.text: Distance above the 200-week SMA at each confirmation: +220% (2014), +222% (2018), +42% (2019), +12% (2020), +120% (2022), +73% (2025). BTC on Nov 13: 0.9% above it
facts.source: computed from blockchain.com average daily prices, and Yahoo closes for Nov 13

facts.text: The Mar 22 2020 confirmation: 6,190, and 52 weeks later +838%
facts.source: computed from blockchain.com average daily prices

careful: March 2020 is one precedent, and it was a COVID crash. Say 'last time', never 'this time it will'.
4 of those 6 went another 37 to 61% lower. That is why Sunday matters, so say it too.

topics.title: Why it's falling this week: Nvidia, Anthropic and the Fed
topics.why_now: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12, Anthropic's IPO is expected next week, and traders now price a December rate hike.
topics.angle: One tab, three reasons, then move on. Money is being pulled toward AI and away from risk. That is a liquidity story, not a 'Bitcoin is broken' story.

tabs.label: CoinDesk: Bitcoin plunges to $68,000 as Anthropic IPO frenzy adds to market jitters
highlights: investor capital headed into Anthropic as well as a broader risk-off move
prompts: Three things hit at once. Jensen Huang quit Nvidia. Anthropic is about to do one of the biggest IPOs ever. And the market thinks the Fed hikes in December.
Xapo Bank's CEO thinks people are selling Bitcoin to free up cash for that IPO. Makes sense. Bitcoin is the thing you can sell at 3am on a Saturday.

facts.text: Nvidia: Huang 'resigned as president, chief executive and board member' on Nov 12, and shares 'fell as much as 14%' that day. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO
Anthropic 'aims to raise up to $64.4 billion', at 'a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion', with orders for 'roughly six times the shares available' (Bloomberg). Expected next week
CME FedWatch: 'an 88% chance of a 25-basis-point increase' at the December meeting. 'The Dollar Index rose above 103, its highest since April 2025.' $1.64 billion liquidated in 24 hours (CoinGlass)

careful: The article itself says it is 'hard to pin the drop solely on the IPO'. Say the IPO is adding pressure, not that it is the cause.
Nvidia's 14% was intraday, not the close. Skip the personal stories around Huang entirely.

topics.title: Who's selling, and who was buying
topics.why_now: Short-term holders sent around 47,300 BTC to exchanges at a loss in one day and the ETFs lost $1.44B in five days, while JPMorgan's filing shows it added Bitcoin exposure through September.
topics.angle: The newest buyers are handing their coins over. That is what a shakeout looks like: coins move from the people who panic to the people with a plan.

tabs.label: Decrypt: Bitcoin short-term holders send $3.6 billion in BTC to exchanges at a loss
highlights: roughly 47,300 BTC transferred to exchanges below their acquisition price over 24 hours
prompts: Look at this. The people who bought in the last few months sent around 47,000 Bitcoin to exchanges in one day. At a loss.
And who was stacking? JPMorgan. Close to a billion dollars in Bitcoin ETFs, Strategy and Coinbase by the end of September.
inspiring: Every time, the coins move from the people who panic to the people with a plan. Which one are you going to be?

facts.text: CryptoQuant, via Decrypt: 'roughly 47,300 BTC transferred to exchanges below their acquisition price over 24 hours', near the deepest reading since July
Spot Bitcoin ETFs: 'five straight days of net outflows totaling $1.44 billion' (SoSoValue)
JPMorgan 'held roughly $981 million across spot Bitcoin ETFs, Michael Saylor's Strategy, and crypto exchange Coinbase as of Sept. 30', $540 million of it in IBIT

careful: The JPMorgan numbers are its Sept 30 filing, before this drop. Say 'by the end of September', never 'JPMorgan is buying this dip'.
CryptoQuant shows transfers to exchanges, not completed sales. Say 'sent to exchanges'.

topics.angle: Your own line from the stream: you buy in the fear. Use July 1 as the 'last time', and keep it a feeling, not a timing signal.

tabs.label: Fear and Greed Index (CoinMarketCap)
tabs.show: Read today's number, then hover the chart back to Sep 22 and to Jun 30 and Jul 1.
prompts: Seven weeks ago this was 78. Greed. Everybody was euphoric. Today it's 18. Extreme fear. Same people, same coins.
The last time it was this low was July 1. The day after this year's low. From there Bitcoin went up 44% in under three months.
inspiring: You buy in the fear. You definitely buy in the fear.
You've looked at old charts and asked how anybody didn't buy there. This is what it feels like from the inside.

facts.text: CoinMarketCap Fear and Greed: 18 (Extreme Fear) on Nov 13, 78 on Sep 22
The last reading this low: 18 on Jul 1 2026 (16 on Jun 30, the day of the 2026 low close). BTC was 60,004 on Jul 1 and 86,603 on Sep 21, +44%
facts.source: computed from CoinMarketCap's index data and BTC daily closes (Yahoo)

careful: Fear alone is not a timing signal: since 2018, on days the alternative.me index was 31 or lower, BTC 90 days later had a median of -2.0% (dataset entry fear-greed-flip). July is 'last time', never a promise.
Indexes differ: alternative.me reads 20 and CoinDesk printed 19. Read the CoinMarketCap number on your tab.

topics.title: Wall Street keeps building: DTCC adds Solana
topics.why_now: DTCC said on Nov 12 it will bring its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027, after going live on Canton and its own Besu chain on Oct 28.
topics.angle: Price is falling and the plumbing keeps getting built. You liked the DTCC 0.1% post, and this is the fresh DTCC news. It also ties back to your Canton video.

tabs.label: CoinDesk: DTCC adds Solana to Wall Street tokenization plans, targeting 2027 rollout
highlights: bring its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027
Through its DTC subsidiary, it holds $114 trillion in securities for banks and brokerages.
prompts: While everybody's staring at the price, look at what's happening underneath. DTCC, the company that holds 114 trillion dollars in securities, is bringing tokenized stocks and Treasuries to Solana.
It went live on Canton at the end of October. Stellar and Circle's Arc come next year. Wall Street isn't leaving crypto. It's moving in.

facts.text: DTCC will 'bring its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027': eligible stocks, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries
Live since Oct 28 on the Canton Network and DTCC's private Besu chain. Stellar and Circle's Arc are expected in 2027
DTC holds $114 trillion in securities. The roughly $30 trillion figure going around is what is eligible for tokenization, 'not the amount already onchain'

careful: The tokens move only between registered DTC participant wallets, a 'walled garden' (Cointelegraph). 20 participants have signed up and none has said it will use Solana. Never 'Wall Street is buying SOL'.
Solana is not in your stack, so keep this about the plumbing, not a SOL pitch.
